1 ثَمَلَ , [aor., app.,
ثَمِلَ and
ثَمُلَ ,] inf. n. ثَمْلٌ, It (water) remained in a watering-trough or tank. (Msb.) ―
-b2- Also, (T, TA,) aor.
ثَمِلَ and
ثَمُلَ , (TK,) inf. n. ثَمْلٌ (T, M, K) and ثُمُولٌ, (M, K,) He (a man, T) remained, stayed, resided, dwelt, or tarried. (T, M, K.) You say, ثَمَلَ فُلَانٌ فَمَا يَبْرَحُ Such a one remained, &c., and does not quit his place. (T.) And ارْتَحَلَ بَنُو فُلَانٍ وَثَمَلَ فُلَانٌ فِى دَارِهِمْ, i. e., [The sons of such a one removed, or departed, and such a one] remained [in their abode]. (T, TA.) ＝
-A2- ثَمَلَهُ He steeped it, or macerated it, and left it, or kept it, long; namely, poison. (Skr p. 194.) [See ثُمَالٌ.] ―
-b2- ثَمَلَتِ الصِّبْيَانَ, aor.
ثَمِلَ , [inf. n., app., ثَمْلٌ,] She (a woman) was a support to the children, remaining, or abiding, with them. (M.) And ثَمَلَهُمْ, (T, M, K,) aor.
ثَمُلَ (T, K) and
ثَمِلَ , (K,) inf. n. تَمْلٌ, (M,) He aided them, or succoured them, (T, K,) namely, his party, kinsfolk, or tribe, (K,) and undertook, or managed, their affairs: (Ibn-Buzurj, T, K:) he fed them, and gave them drink, (M, K,) namely, orphans, (M,) and undertook, or managed, their affairs. (M, K.) ―
-b3- مَا ثَمَلَ شَرَابَهُ بِشَىْءٍ (Yoo, T, S, M, K) مِنْ طَعَامٍ (Yoo, S) He ate no food before drinking. (Yoo, T, S, M, K.) ―
-b4- You say also, أَكَلَتِ المَاشِيَةُ مِنَ الكَلَأِ مَا يَثْمُلُ مَا فِى أَجْوَافِهَا مِنَ المَآءِ The cattle ate of the herbage what was equal to the water that they had drunk. (T.) ―
-b5- And ثَمَلَ, aor.
ثَمِلَ , He ate (K) food. (TK.) ＝
-A3- ثَمِلَ, (S, M, K,) aor.
ثَمَلَ , (K,) inf. n. ثَمَلٌ, (S, M, K, *) He (a man, S) became intoxicated. (S, M, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
